key_insight: DynThinker shows that strong spatial intelligence requires balancing static 3D and dynamic 4D reasoning instead of optimizing one at the expense of the other. The paper finds this tradeoff is not uniform across the network, with late-layer parameters being especially important for maintaining both abilities.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the challenge that current models cannot reliably handle both static 3D spatial reasoning and dynamic 4D reasoning at the same time. Improving one often weakens the other, making it hard to build general-purpose spatial models.
method: Analyze where 3D-4D interference occurs across different parameter groups in the model.
Identify which layers are most sensitive to the static-vs-dynamic balance, especially in later layers.
Use this understanding to guide a unified evaluation and reasoning framework for both static and dynamic spatial tasks.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work provides a clearer roadmap for building spatial models that generalize across both worlds and motion. It can help avoid training strategies that accidentally degrade one capability while improving another.
visual_elements: Split-screen 3D vs 4D comparison showing static scenes and moving scenes
Heatmap of parameter sensitivity across model layers, highlighting late layers
Tradeoff curve illustrating static accuracy versus dynamic accuracy
Icon-based pipeline showing analysis, interference discovery, and unified reasoning
paper_title: DynThinker: Unifying Static 3D and Dynamic 4D Spatial Reasoning
paper_authors: Qihang Cao, Haoyuan Li, Zihan Guo, Sensen Gao, Zihui Gao
